oauth.alternatives: Sign in with Slack (OIDC) only gives identity, not message access. Use the v2 OAuth flow for agents.

appTypes.name: Single-workspace (undistributed) app
appTypes.whenToUse: Only for your own workspace or internal tools. Not for an agent product.

appTypes.name: Unlisted distributed app
appTypes.whenToUse: Fits an agent product at first. Any workspace can install through OAuth after you click Activate Public Distribution. No review, but history reads are throttled.

appTypes.name: Slack Marketplace app
appTypes.whenToUse: Use when you need normal rate limits on conversations.history and conversations.replies, or a public listing. Needs Slack review.

appTypes.name: Org-level (Enterprise Grid) app
appTypes.whenToUse: Use for Enterprise customers who want one install across an org. Needs org_deploy_enabled and may need an Org Admin.

verdict.label: Self-serve, optional review
verdict.summary: Any workspace can install an unlisted distributed Slack app with no review, but non-Marketplace apps get 1 request per minute and 15 messages on conversations.history and conversations.replies. Workspace admins can also require approval before install.
verdict.nextStep: Create an app at https://api.slack.com/apps, add your HTTPS redirect URL and scopes, then click Activate Public Distribution.
verdict.customerSideGateNote: Some workspaces limit installs to admins, require admin approval requests, or allow only Marketplace-listed apps.

composio.note: Composio lists Slack under managed OAuth, so you can start today. Moving to your own Slack app later only affects new connections. Existing users must reconnect.

stages.name: Prototype
stages.whoCanConnect: Your development workspace. Composio managed app works for any workspace meanwhile.
stages.notes: Create the app and install it to one workspace with one click.

stages.name: Unlisted distribution
stages.whoCanConnect: Any Slack workspace that can install the app. Admin approval may apply.
stages.notes: Needs OAuth flow, HTTPS URLs, and the distribution checklist. Message history reads are throttled for non-Marketplace apps.

stages.name: Slack Marketplace listing
stages.whoCanConnect: Anyone, with direct install from the listing and normal rate limits.
stages.notes: Optional for connecting, but needed for full history rate limits. Review time not confirmed.

scopeTiers.name: Bot and basic scopes
scopeTiers.effect: Install works without review. Least risk of admin pushback.

scopeTiers.name: Message history scopes
scopeTiers.effect: No review to install, but conversations.history and conversations.replies are capped at 1 request per minute and 15 objects for non-Marketplace apps. Marketplace approval lifts this.

scopeTiers.name: Broad or restricted scopes
scopeTiers.effect: Slack lists these as reasons an app may be unsuitable for the Marketplace unless a clear need exists. Unlisted use still installs.

scopeTiers.name: Offline access (token rotation)
scopeTiers.effect: Tokens do not expire by default. Optional rotation gives 12 hour tokens plus refresh tokens. It cannot be turned off once on.

requirements.item: Slack account and a workspace you own
requirements.detail: Sign in at api.slack.com/apps and pick a development workspace.

requirements.item: HTTPS redirect URL, events and interactivity URLs
requirements.detail: SSL is required for all OAuth redirect and request URLs on distributed apps. Redirect must be HTTPS.
Under Manage Distribution, finish the checklist, then Activate Public Distribution.

requirements.item: Marketplace listing assets and policy compliance
requirements.detail: Name, descriptions, icon, 1600x1000 screenshots, optional video, plus App Developer Policy, Marketplace Agreement, API Terms and security review. At least 10 active workspaces and 10 weekly active users.

steps.title: Create the Slack app
steps.detail: Go to https://api.slack.com/apps, click Create New App, choose From manifest or From scratch, name it, and pick your dev workspace.

steps.title: Set redirect URL and scopes
steps.detail: Under OAuth & Permissions add an HTTPS Redirect URL and the smallest bot and user scopes you need. Use user_scope for acting as the user.

steps.title: Build the OAuth exchange
steps.detail: Send users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with client_id, scope, user_scope, redirect_uri and state. Exchange the code (valid 10 minutes) at oauth.v2.access.

steps.title: Decide on token rotation
steps.detail: Turn on token rotation under OAuth & Permissions if you want 12 hour tokens. Store the new refresh token on every refresh. It cannot be turned off later.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: In Manage Distribution, complete the checklist and click Activate Public Distribution to get an Add to Slack link.

steps.title: Plan for admin approval
steps.detail: Build a message for users whose workspace blocks installs, and ask them to send an admin approval request. Request few scopes.

steps.title: Design around history throttling
steps.detail: Use Events API for new messages and cache. Do not plan on bulk history reads while unlisted: 1 request a minute, 15 messages.

steps.title: Check Marketplace fit
steps.detail: Read the submission guidelines. Avoid disallowed patterns such as data export, LLM training on Slack data, MCP-only apps, or restricted scopes.

steps.title: Prepare listing and submit
steps.detail: Write descriptions, make screenshots, record an optional 30 to 90 second video of the production app, then submit from the app dashboard.

steps.title: Wait for Slack review
steps.detail: Respond to review feedback. Timeline is not stated in the pages read.

steps.title: Migrate from Composio managed app
steps.detail: Swap in your client ID and secret in Composio. Ask existing users to reconnect.

blockers.symptom: conversations.history returns only 15 messages and rate limits after one call per minute
blockers.cause: Non-Marketplace distributed apps were moved to Tier 1 limits. New apps from May 29, 2025, existing apps later.
blockers.fix: Use Events API and caching, get Marketplace approval, or use an internal customer-built app inside the customer's own workspace.
blockers.escalation: Slack developer support or the Slack developer changelog

blockers.symptom: User cannot install, or sees an approval request screen
blockers.cause: Workspace restricts installs to admins, requires approval, or allows only Marketplace apps.
blockers.fix: Ask the user to send the request to an admin. Reduce scopes. Marketplace listing helps with Marketplace-only workspaces.

blockers.cause: Redirect not HTTPS, not matching a configured Redirect URL, or redirect_uri differs between authorize and access steps.
blockers.fix: Use HTTPS and send the identical redirect_uri in both steps.

blockers.symptom: Refresh fails on second use, or tokens revoked
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens are single use. More than 2 active tokens revokes the oldest.
blockers.fix: Persist each new refresh token and refresh once per cycle.

blockers.cause: Restricted or broad scopes, too few active workspaces, data export, or not fully tested.
blockers.fix: Cut scopes, reach 10 active workspaces and 10 weekly active users, and fix listed issues.
blockers.escalation: Slack Marketplace team via submission feedback

blockers.symptom: App is removed from a workspace
blockers.cause: Apps with broader scopes are uninstalled when the installing user leaves or becomes a guest.
blockers.fix: Have a long-lived admin install, and handle app_uninstalled events.

drafts.title: Scope justification
drafts.body: Our assistant helps users triage Slack messages. We request channels:history, groups:history and im:history so it can read messages in conversations the user chose. We request chat:write so it can post replies the user approves. We do not use Slack data to train models. We do not export messages. Users can disconnect at any time, and we delete stored data on uninstall.

drafts.title: Demo video script (30 to 90 seconds)
drafts.body: 1. Show the production app and the Add to Slack button. 2. Show the consent screen with scopes. 3. Show the app reading a message in a real-looking channel. 4. Show the assistant drafting and posting a reply. 5. Show disconnect and data deletion. Use realistic names, captions on, no ads.

uncertainties.question: How long does Slack Marketplace review take?
uncertainties.why: The pages read do not state a timeline and no developer reports were checked.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Read the Marketplace review guide on docs.slack.dev or ask Slack developer support.

uncertainties.question: Does Slack support PKCE?
uncertainties.why: Docs read describe client secret exchange only and the OIDC discovery lists no PKCE methods.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Search Slack docs for PKCE or test a code_challenge.

uncertainties.question: What are the exact current limits for existing non-Marketplace apps?
uncertainties.why: Sources disagree on dates: Slack states Sept 2, 2025, a community post says March 3, 2026. Rate limit pages were seen only as search results.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Open https://docs.slack.dev/changelog/2025/05/29/rate-limit-changes-for-non-marketplace-apps/ and the rate limits page.

uncertainties.question: Is the 10 workspace minimum a hard rule for agent products?
uncertainties.why: The guideline says apps below it are unsuitable, which makes first listing a chicken and egg problem.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Ask the Marketplace team before submitting.
